text.p: HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - Production in the chemical industry in 1996 totalled 38.59 billion crowns, a year-on-year increase of some three percent. Exports rose by 0.6 percent, year-on-year, and totalled 25.1 billion crowns.
- Japanese electronics firm Sony and car cabling cystem producer Yazaki said they both planned to expand their Slovak activities, which began last year.

- Prime Minister Vladimir Meciar, currently in Japan on an official visit, has offered investment bank Nomura the opportunity to finance construction of a car maker in Slovakia, which would then export its production to Ukraine and Russia.
NARODNA OBRODA - The forthcoming referenda on Slovakia's NATO membership and direct presidential elections, scheduled for May 23 and 24, will cost the state some 147 million crowns.
- Multinational home appliance producer Eletrolux said it planned to gain about a 25 percent market share in Slovakia by the year 2000.

PRAVDA - The Finance Ministry has approved a decrease in maximum allowed motor fuel prices, effective April 1. The price of petrol will ease by 0.30 crowns a litre, while the price of diesel oil will be lower by 0.10 crowns a litre.

- Some 20,009 employees of steel producer VSZ have joined the newly-created trade union Metalurg, which plans to join the Slovak Confederation of Trade Unions. Until now, all workers in the steel and enegineering industry were members of the largest industrial trade union, OZ KOVO.

- Stefan Balejik, head of the Highest Control Bureau (NKU), said the NKU is capable of carrying out a deep audit of state -controlled banks, as requested by a coalition member, the Workers Party (ZRS), if the government, the parliament and the central bank's governing board approve such a move.

- Balejik criticised the fact that the National Property Fund (NPF), the state privatisation agency, was still outside the control of the NKU. He said the law on the NKU would have to be revised to allow more effective controlling of the state institutions.

- Police found two unspecified explosives in one of the largest sport halls in Bratislava on Tuesday night, just after the end of a meeting of members and supporters of the opposition Christian Democratic Movement (KDH).
